item: Official market betting lines
detail: Reconciled. Real prices now exist, but they are NOT official and they are NOT in this register's scope: the NFL publishes no betting lines, so no price on this site is official. One licensed book's prices (DraftKings, published by ESPN) were captured for 29 games - open and close, spread, total and moneyline - and are on the Market & price archive page. Every one of those rows carries two links: the NFL.com game page that proves the result, and the ESPN odds resource the price was archived from. A second, independently taken capture of the same prices (14 games) fills the market columns on the model-lines and price-snapshot pages; the two captures agree on all 112 comparable numbers, which tools/reconcile_prices.py re-derives and the publication gate enforces. What remains unverified is any price for a player prop or a prop combination: no official or licensed source was confirmed for those, so those cells are still blank (F-35).
why: The capture is a transcription of one book's published numbers at a timestamped moment, not an official league figure and not a market consensus. It is sufficient to compute a backtest, a ROI and a closing-line value against a real price; it is not sufficient to claim a price is the best available, that a line is official, or that an arbitrage exists between books. Those claims are not made.

item: Depth-chart string: starter, 2nd, 3rd, 4th
detail: This was open in the first build: no player on the site was assigned a depth position, because nfl.com/teams/<club>/depth-chart returns HTTP 404 for every club. It is now closed from an official source. Each club's own official website publishes its depth chart as an ordered table, and the column order is the depth position - first name in a row = starter, second = backup, third = third string. 31 of the 32 clubs publish a machine-readable ordered chart, and all 1,558 depth rows are on the Depth & deficiency page with a link to the club page each one came from.
why: The league publishes no consolidated chart, but the clubs are the authority on their own depth and they publish it themselves. Recording the ordering the club itself prints is a transcription, not an inference: no rank is assigned where the club does not print one, co-starters are kept as co-starters, and a club that publishes its chart only as an image (Houston) is left blank and flagged as F-18 instead of being guessed at.

item: Players on injured reserve, PUP and NFI
detail: The public Week 10 injury page omits players on IR/PUP/NIR. Baltimore's starting quarterback, for example, appears only in league news.
why: Any availability model built from the public page alone will silently miss long-term absences, which are exactly the absences that move a line.

item: Two official sources give different absence windows for the same player
detail: One NFL.com item says the Ravens' Lamar Jackson is out 6-9 weeks; another says the Ravens confirm he is expected to miss 6-10 weeks.
why: Both are official league sources and they disagree. Neither is corrected on this site; the conflict is recorded so the discrepancy can be resolved by the club or the league before either figure is used.

item: Player-level game logs, snaps, drives and EPA
detail: No player-level season statistics are published here.
why: The official free pages fetched for this build did not expose a complete player-level dataset in a verifiable form. Player-prop strategies therefore remain framework only, with no measured performance.

item: Player-prop and parlay strategy performance
detail: No player-prop strategy, no parlay price and no combined-bet performance figure is published.
why: Pricing a combination requires a joint distribution over player outcomes, which depends on F-02 and F-05. Publishing a number now would be a guess presented as a measurement.

item: No strategy has passed all seven validation gates
detail: Across 105 out-of-sample games the best strategy's improvement over the league-constant benchmark has a Bonferroni-adjusted bootstrap interval that still contains zero.
why: This is the gate doing its job. A leaderboard that ranked strategies by point estimate alone would have declared a winner that the evidence does not support.

item: Model parameters have no official source
detail: The decay factors, shrinkage weights, bootstrap settings and gate thresholds are analyst choices made by this project.
why: They are the first thing a reviewer should challenge, and changing any of them changes the ranking. They are published in full on the Methodology page so they can be argued with.

item: NFL.com deep links of the form /schedules/2026/REG<n>/ silently redirect to the current week
detail: The URL pattern that appears to address an individual week resolves to whichever week is live.
why: Any automation built on that pattern would silently re-read the current week instead of the requested one. The working per-week pattern is /schedules/2026/by-week/week-<n>, which was confirmed directly for weeks 5 and 11.

item: Weeks 12 to 18 of the 2026 schedule are not published here
detail: Only the completed Weeks 1-10 games and the official Week 11 schedule are published.
why: NFL itself lists several late-season matchups as to-be-determined, and the league's own notice explains that those dates, times and networks are only fixed later in the season.

item: Injury-report policy link carried over from an earlier session was not re-verified
detail: The Competition Committee injury-report policy link recorded by an earlier session was not re-fetched during this build.
why: It is left in the repository as recorded by the session that verified it, and is not re-certified here. Nothing published on this site depends on it.

item: Repository hygiene at the start of this build
detail: Before this work the repository contained exactly one tracked file - a four-byte README - with no licence, no contributing guide, no continuous integration, no tests, no data and no site.
why: Recorded for the audit trail. This build adds the verified datasets, the verification harness, the model engine and continuous integration that checks the site and the data before publication.

item: The published site exists in two copies that could drift apart
detail: GitHub Pages is configured to serve the repository root, while the publish workflow uploads the site/ directory as its artifact. If the two copies differ, a reader sees different numbers depending on which build served the page.
why: The root is now a byte-identical mirror of site/ and of the X4 Console in docs/, the publish workflow checks the mirror before it uploads, and the check step was re-run locally against the committed tree with exit code 0. The first version of that check failed on a clean checkout because it compared the build tools check.py and check.js as if they were site assets; both are now excluded.

item: The same two clubs are labelled differently in the two layers
detail: NFL.com's own standings page labels the Los Angeles Rams LA and the Arizona Cardinals AZ. The main dataset keys them LAR and ARI - the abbreviations NFL.com itself uses in its game-page URLs - while the decision-desk layer keys them LA and AZ.
why: No value is wrong, but a reviewer comparing the two layers would otherwise read the same club as two teams. The mapping is written out explicitly in the desk generator rather than inferred, and the two independent transcriptions were compared club by club: all 32 agree on wins, losses, ties, points for, points allowed and net points.

item: The X4 Console's no-JavaScript fallback counts were stale
detail: The console landing page printed 26 facts and 15 flagged items in the text that renders when JavaScript is unavailable, while the data files those counters are generated from hold 27 executive-summary facts and 16 flagged items.
why: A reader without JavaScript would have been told the register was one item shorter than it is. The fallback text now matches the data; both numbers were counted from the data files rather than read off the page.

item: Two different flagged registers reuse the same identifiers
detail: This site and the decision-desk layer each publish a flagged register, and both number their entries F-01, F-02, F-03 ... for different items. F-02 on the main site is the depth-chart gap; F-02 on the desk layer is the missing calibration metrics.
why: The two registers were built by parallel sessions working from the same brief, and neither knew the other's numbering. They have been left as they are and cross-referenced from the landing-page directory rather than renumbered, because renumbering one register would invalidate the cross-references the other already publishes.

item: The three published layers define three different validation gates
detail: The Strategy Lab on this site scores seven gates (G1 data integrity, G2 out-of-sample, G3 minimum sample, G4 significance, G5 stability, G6 calibration, G7 not the benchmark). The decision-desk layer specifies eight (adding probability quality, economic performance, multiplicity control, parlay and prop integrity, and a shadow period). The X4 Console specifies nine (G0 to G8). No two layers use the same inventory.
why: The main site's seven are the gates that can actually be scored from the official data that exists; the other two are written as designs for gates that cannot yet be evaluated. A reader comparing the layers would reasonably ask which inventory is authoritative, so each layer states its own count on its own page and the difference is recorded here rather than left to be discovered.

item: Official injury-report drift on two practice-status cells
detail: The committed Week-10 injury dataset records Greg Van Roten (G, NE) and Charles Woods (CB, NE) as Limited participation. The live official NFL.com injury report, re-fetched 2026-11-14 by the new live-verification harness (tools/verify_live.py), shows both as Full Participation in Practice. The league updates the report during the week, so the committed cells reflect an earlier snapshot.
why: SUPERSEDED on 2026-11-15 by F-41: the injury dataset was re-captured from the live official page and regenerated through the pipeline. The text below records the state on 2026-11-14. The committed data was deliberately not changed then - editing it would fork the published numbers away from the snapshot the rest of the build was verified against. Both values and both source links are recorded here and on the decision-desk register (R-14) so the drift can be reviewed and, if the current snapshot is adopted, regenerated through the normal pipeline rather than hand-patched. This entry records the two cells this session's live harness caught; F-29 records the broader set of practice-status moves found by a parallel live verification, and the two are complementary, not duplicate.

item: Market betting lines are not an official NFL publication
detail: The league publishes no betting lines. The market columns on this site are therefore filled from a captured feed - DraftKings prices read through the ESPN odds endpoint on 2026-11-14 - and every such figure is labelled with that provenance. The store on this page holds 14 games (the 13 official Week 11 games and the one final Week 10 game) across 12 phase cells each - 168 cells in total, of which 116 carry a price and 52 are genuinely empty because the closing phase is reserved for a game that has actually been played and 13 of the 14 games have not.
why: A market column is required by the brief and no official source exists for one, so the honest options are to publish nothing or to publish a clearly-labelled non-official price next to the official game identity. This site does the second: the price is never presented as an NFL line, the source is printed in the row, and the difference column (fair minus market) is published as its own column so a disagreement is never read as an edge. Where the feed had no price, the cell stays blank and says so.

item: Staking / bankroll figures
detail: No staking, bankroll, Kelly or position-sizing figure is published for any strategy. The staking column of the leaderboard is blank.
why: Staking requires market prices and bankroll rules. With no licensed odds feed, no staking figure can be computed, which is exactly what keeps a lucky staking run from masquerading as signal.

item: ROI and expected-value figures
detail: No ROI, expected value or parlay price is published for any bet, combination or player prop.
why: ROI needs a settled result (available in the verified results feed) AND a price at which the bet was taken (not available, see F-18). Until a price feed is authorised, ROI cells stay blank rather than be invented.

item: Replacement depth: starter, 2nd, 3rd, 4th string
detail: No player on this site is assigned a replacement depth. The replacement-depth table records who replaced whom and why, but the depth column is blank for every row.
why: The NFL publishes no consolidated league depth chart that labels 1st/2nd/3rd/4th string, so any depth rank would be an invention. The fact of a replacement is tracked from league reporting; the depth of that replacement is not.

item: Demotion gate basis
detail: The demotion gate (live strategy -> paper trading) is a project design choice, not an official NFL rule.
why: No league or regulator publishes a demotion gate for betting strategies. The gate's thresholds (5-game rolling window, 0.12 calibration gap, 10-game paper return) are analyst choices and should be challenged before any live use.

item: Price-snapshot store values are model estimates, not official lines
detail: The price-snapshot store records the opening and closing fair lines we originate for each market. The opening values are model estimates (S3 recommended line) derived from official NFL.com results; the closing values are blank until the games close.
why: Because we originate our own lines, the snapshot store is our own record. It is not a market observation and must not be read as an official or sportsbook line.

item: The Houston Texans publish their depth chart only as an image
detail: houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart renders its chart as a single bitmap image with no table markup and no ordered text, so no Houston depth position can be transcribed from it. Houston is the only club of the 32 with no rows on the Depth & deficiency page.
why: The five Houston players the official NFL injury report rules Out or Doubtful for Week 10 (Azeez Al-Shaair, Marvin Harrison Jr., Danielle Hunter, Brevin Jordan, Keylan Rutledge) therefore have no published depth position on this site. Reading a rank off a picture would be an eyeball inference, so those cells are blank and the five names are listed as unmatched instead.

item: 20 officially ruled-out or doubtful players do not appear on their own club's published depth chart
detail: Of the 81 players the official Week 10 injury report lists as Out or Doubtful (70 Out, 11 Doubtful), 62 appear on their club's published depth chart (61 by exact name, plus one name-only match flagged in F-42) and 20 do not: Lucas Patrick (WAS), Kerby Joseph (DET), Omarr Norman-Lott (KC), Micah Parsons (GB), BJ Green II (JAX), Tommy Townsend (TEN), Luke Rhodes (IND), Jonathon Brooks and Mike Jackson (CAR), Terrance Ferguson (LAR), Zachary Carter (ARI), Jalen Davis, Andrei Iosivas and Brian Parker II (CIN), Isas Waxter (LAC), plus the five Houston players above.
why: A club's depth chart is editorial and lags roster moves, so an absent name is not evidence the player is not on the team. The effect on this site is conservative: those 20 absences are counted in the official injury totals but not in the depth-based starter-out score, so the starter-out figures are a floor, not a ceiling. Each is listed by name on the Depth & deficiency page so a reviewer can chase them individually. (The count was 19 of 76 before the 2026-11-15 re-capture in F-41.)

item: Clubs disagree on what a depth chart is, and some say so in writing
detail: The Patriots state that their chart 'is unofficial and is published by the writers of Patriots.com' and does not necessarily reflect the organization's view. The Jets and Eagles say theirs is compiled by their communications departments. The Chiefs, Vikings, Rams, Titans, Bears, Bengals and Cardinals stamp a date on theirs (10-31 to 11-10); the others do not. Section and position labels differ club to club - DL / DT / NT / EDGE / RUSH / LOLB / WILL / MIKE / SAM / NCB / NICKEL / DB.
why: The ordering is official in the sense that the club publishes it, but it is editorial rather than a league record, and its vintage varies by up to a fortnight. No attempt is made here to reconcile the label vocabularies into a single taxonomy; each row keeps the club's own position label, so a reviewer sees exactly what the club printed. The date each club stamps is shown where one exists and left blank where the club stamps none.

item: A published depth chart is not proof of who started
detail: Nothing in this dataset records who actually took the first snap. A club can list a player first and start someone else; snap counts and official game books would settle it, and neither is captured here.
why: The starter-out score therefore measures listed depth, not realised participation. It is a pre-game availability signal, which is what a line is set from, but it cannot be used as a post-game explanation of a result without the game books. The suggestion queue ranks game-book ingestion as the fix.

item: Only two position rows have no published replacement, and no row has both starter and backup out
detail: Tennessee is the only club where a listed starter is ruled out at a position where the club names nobody behind him: left guard Peter Skoronski and linebacker Cody Barton. No club has both its listed starter and its listed backup ruled out at the same position for Week 10.
why: This is a negative result and it is published because it constrains the strategy work: the '2nd and 3rd string replace the starter' cascade that the brief asks to detect cannot be found in the official Week 10 data at all, so any model that assumes a cascade is happening would be inventing it. The detection is in place for the weeks where it does occur.

item: Four practice statuses moved between the committed injury snapshot and the 2026-11-14 read
detail: tools/build.py reads data/injuries-wk10-2026.csv. Re-reading the official NFL.com injury report on 2026-11-14 for eight clubs (101 players, 404 practice-status fields) found four cells that no longer match: Houston's Montgomery and Jaylin Smith are now Full where the snapshot says Limited, Cleveland's Denzel Ward is now Limited where the snapshot says Full, and Arizona's Andrew Wingard is now DNP where the snapshot says Limited.
why: The snapshot was not overwritten. Both transcriptions are committed (research/verification/injuries-week10-2026-11-14-session-4e108e9a.csv) so a reader can see the drift rather than a silently corrected number. An earlier version of this flag described three drifts and 401 of 404 fields because it was computed from a four-club subset; the eight-club re-read found four, and the smaller number is the wrong one.

item: No official closing line can exist, so the closing snapshot is stored empty
detail: A closing line is the last price before kickoff. Every Week 11 game is still in the future, so no closing line exists for any of the 39 registered closing rows. The rows are stored with every price cell blank rather than omitted or back-filled.
why: Storing the row and leaving it blank is the difference between 'not yet observed' and 'not tracked'. Back-filling it with the current price would produce a column that looks like data and is a guess. It also means closing-line value cannot be computed yet, which is stated on the results page rather than worked around.

item: The opening snapshot records points, not the price on those points
detail: The opening spread and total are recorded as points (-1.0, 43.5). The american price attached to those points at the open (-110, -105, +100) is not part of the same published payload, so the opening rows carry a line without a price on it.
why: Points and prices are different numbers and a strategy can be right about one and wrong about the other. An opening line at -110 and the same line at +100 are not the same bet. Recording the points alone is truthful; attaching an assumed -110 would not be.

item: The publication gate rejected the surname Fagnano as a placeholder marker
detail: site/check.py ran a case-insensitive substring search for a three-letter not-a-number placeholder marker over every published page. The row naming the Ravens' third-string quarterback - Joe Fagnano, as stated by nfl.com news - contains those three letters and failed the build. The page was correct and the checker was wrong.
why: Recorded rather than silently fixed because it is a failure mode worth knowing about: a substring placeholder test will eventually collide with a real word, and the collision produces a build failure that looks like a data problem but is not. The fix is a word-boundary match on that one marker, with the other markers left as substrings. The alternative - renaming the player - would have put an inaccurate name on the site to satisfy a checker.

item: The depth register on this site contradicted the official injury report for four of its seven rows
detail: data/replacement-depth.csv, merged in with PR #21, has seven rows and all seven are marked verified=unverified. Four of them name a replacement without naming who he replaced: Cleveland (Watson), Arizona (Beck), the Rams (Puka Nacua) and Green Bay (Josh Jacobs). Two more are wrong on their face. The Rams row lists Puka Nacua as a replacement_in, but the official Week 10 injury report also in this repository records Nacua as DNP - did not participate - so he is not a replacement for anyone that week. The Green Bay row lists Josh Jacobs as a replacement_in, but the nfl.com article cited in the same row is the report that Jacobs himself is having finger surgery: he is the starter who is out, not the man coming in. The replacement_depth column, which is the one number the whole register exists to carry, is blank on all seven rows.
why: Flagged rather than quietly overwritten, because the register is on a published page and the contradiction is with official data already in this repository. The corrected chains are on the gates page, where each link is quoted and the starter is named, so the accurate version is already live and the reader can compare. The discrepancy is: this register says Jacobs is the replacement for a blank starter; the article it links says Jacobs is the injured starter.

item: Player-prop and prop-combination prices
detail: No player-prop price, prop line or prop-combination correlation is published. The 174 captured prices cover only the three game markets - spread, total and moneyline - for 29 games.
why: A prop price needs a licensed feed that carries player markets. The one book captured here publishes them, but no timestamped, reversible archive of player props was obtained, and a prop correlation can only be computed from prices that were actually captured. Estimating one would be invention, so the cells are blank. This is the remaining honest gap in the market work, and it is the reason no prop-combination product is priced anywhere on this site.

item: Prices are from one book and are not official
detail: The 174 captured prices on the Market & price archive page come from a single licensed sportsbook (DraftKings, as published by ESPN) at the moment of capture. The NFL publishes no betting lines at all, so no price on this site is an official league figure.
why: A single book's number is a transcription of what that book showed, not a market consensus and not the best available price. It is enough to compute error against a real closing line, a ROI and a closing-line value; it is not enough to claim an arbitrage between books, to claim a price was the best available, or to call a line official. None of those claims is made, and every price row carries both its NFL.com result link and its ESPN odds resource so a reviewer can re-read the number.

item: Doubled HTML entity in the depth summary text
detail: Found by session arena/1b8b6e9e-x4: several phrases in this register and on the landing-page flag preview showed a literal escaped ampersand (the word 'amp;' visible to the reader) because the register strings carried a pre-escaped ampersand into a renderer that escapes text again. Fixed at T31 integration by writing bare ampersands in this register's strings; the pages now render a plain '&' in those phrases.
why: Recorded because it is a failure mode worth knowing about: a text pipeline that escapes in two places produces output that looks like a data error but is not. The strings in this register are rendered through an escaping helper (tools/pages.py flags_table), so they must contain bare text. The alternative - leaving a visible escape sequence on a published page - misleads readers into thinking the underlying label is wrong.

item: The two price stores use the word 'close' differently
detail: The price archive calls the last line the book was showing at the moment of capture 'close', so it is filled for every game, played or not. The integrity store on the price-snapshot page calls that same number 'current', and reserves 'close' for the closing line of a game that has actually been played, so it is empty for the 13 games still to come. The numbers agree - 112 of 112 comparable values match between the two captures - but the labels do not.
why: Recorded rather than silently renamed, because the collision is easy to misread: a reader who compares the two pages and sees an empty 'close' in one of them could think a price is missing when it is the same number under another name. The reconciliation table on the Market & price archive page publishes the comparison number by number, and this flag names the difference. Neither store is edited to hide it.

item: Desk rows without an official source link: the row-source gate was not reading row links
detail: The per-row source check in tools/check_site.py recorded each link in the page-level list but never attached it to its table row, so every row was tested as empty and the check passed without testing anything. Found by the source-provenance audit (arena/5092bd99-x4) and fixed at T31 integration. With the check reading row links, 191 desk-table rows on 13 pages had no https link; they were listed one by one in research/verification/row-source-gaps-2026-11-14.csv. They were decision and requirement text, rubric weights, simulation output, programme status, or computed statistics whose inputs were not linked row by row. None of them was a sourced official value that the page presented as confirmed. A second gap of the same kind was in the price store: 26 spread and total points in the 2026W11-OPEN snapshot of data/market-prices.csv had no source link (their note reads 'points only'); the moneyline rows of that snapshot are all linked.
why: RESOLVED on 2026-11-17 (T41, session arena/550d7436-x4) by line-by-line closure, not by weakening the gate: every one of the 1,045 desk-table rows on 22 pages now carries an https source link, and the checker re-run reports 0 rows without one. NFL-fact rows link to the official NFL page; computed and programme rows cite the committed artifact that produced the value (GitHub blob of the exact CSV/script); blank decision rows cite the official page checked plus the flag. Two honest limits remain, and neither is closed by this fix: (1) the checker verifies link presence, not that a link supports the exact value beside it — a per-value semantic source gate is still open work; (2) the 26 'points only' price rows keep their recorded gap and stay unverified rather than gaining a link that does not support the value. Any reader should still treat a computed row as the artifact's output, not as an official NFL fact.

item: Scheduled official-capture workflow is failing at the fetch step on every recent run (cause unknown)
detail: The six-hourly capture workflow (.github/workflows/capture.yml, added at T37) is intended to keep immutable official snapshots of the injury report and the club depth pages. Its four most recent scheduled runs (44175196682, 44043083196, 43967865851, 43818369872 — Nov 16-17) all failed in 'Fetch, schema-check and store the official pages'; hash verification, freshness and the commit step were skipped, and no data/captures/ history exists in the checkout. The run-log download returned EOF for two independent sessions, so the underlying cause (network, source change, or schema mismatch) is unknown and is not guessed at here. Two confirmed code-path risks from the audit: a partial successful capture is lost because the later steps have no if: always() condition, and freshness is global rather than per source. Full evidence in research/audits/capture-workflow-health-2026-11-17.md (T40, arena/bdf71572-x4).
why: Until the workflow completes a run, the point-in-time availability series is NOT operational: the site's committed datasets remain dated snapshots, and no claim of an automated multi-day capture history may be made. The failure does not affect the published data's own verification, which is tied to the committed captures, and it does not affect the Pages deploy. Clears when: a scheduled run stores a capture and manifest, hash verification passes, and freshness is per source.

item: Ten further injury practice-status cells differ from the official report (reported, not yet independently re-checked)
detail: A parallel session's full capture of the Week 10 injury page (345 of 345 rows) found twelve practice-status cells that differ from data/injuries-wk10-2026.csv. Two are already flagged as F-34 (Greg Van Roten, Charles Woods). The other ten are: Savion Williams (WR, GB), Antonio Johnson (S, JAX), Kaytron Allen (RB, MIA), David Montgomery (RB, HOU), Jaylin Smith (CB, HOU), Denzel Ward (CB, CLE), Andrew Wingard (S, ARI), C.J. West (DT, SF), Von Miller (LB, DAL), Rodney Shelley (CB, LAC). Each row, with its committed value, its live value and its official player page, is in research/verification/live-verification-2026-11-14-e6ee28a8.md.
why: SUPERSEDED on 2026-11-15 by F-41. Nine of these ten reproduce on the live read; Rodney Shelley does not (see F-41). The official report is updated during the week, so the committed snapshot is older than the live page. The committed data is deliberately not edited, so the published numbers stay tied to the snapshot they were verified against. The live values were captured by the parallel session through the platform's web tools; they were not independently re-checked from this sandbox, which cannot reach nfl.com. Recommended: re-run the capture and then regenerate the injury dataset through the normal pipeline, not by hand.

item: Week 10 injury dataset re-captured from the live official NFL.com report: 347 rows, 26 corrected cells, 2 added rows
detail: On 2026-11-15 the official NFL.com Week 10 injury report was read in full (every row of all 28 team sections). The read holds 347 player rows. The committed file held 345. Against it, 26 cells differed in practice or game status, and two Baltimore rows were absent: Calais Campbell (DNP) and Ronnie Stanley (DNP). Twelve of the 26 are in the Chargers section (Kayode Awosika, Bud Dupree, Justin Eboigbe, Ladd McConkey, Keaton Mitchell, David Njoku, Denzel Perryman, Trey Pipkins, Branson Taylor, Brenen Thompson, Isas Waxter, Kendall Williamson). The other fourteen: Van Roten and Woods (NE), Savion Williams (GB), Antonio Johnson (JAX), Kaytron Allen (MIA), Arden Key (IND), David Montgomery and Jaylin Smith (HOU), Denzel Ward (CLE), Andrew Wingard (ARI), C.J. West (SF), Von Miller (DAL), Jaylinn Hawkins and Adam Randall (BAL). The three Detroit designations that were listed as blank (Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed) read Out on the live page and were already Out in the committed file, so no blank remains. Two figures in the brief did not reproduce: the committed file held 345 rows, not 254, and the live page holds 347, not 279. Rodney Shelley (LAC) was recorded as Full-to-Limited on 2026-11-14 (F-40); the live read shows Full, matching the committed value, so that one change is not reproduced. Every corrected value is the value printed on the page, transcribed to research/verification/official-injury-report-wk10-capture-2026-11-15.csv and checked against the committed file by tools/capture_check.py.
why: The live page changes during the week, so the committed file is a dated copy and not a standing fact. The regenerated site now carries the 2026-11-15 read: depth counts, availability rows and the starter-out figures were recomputed by the normal pipeline, not hand-patched. The read was made with the platform's page-fetch tool, which returns the page as text; this sandbox cannot reach nfl.com directly, so the capture is a transcription of that text rather than the raw HTTP bytes. A raw, hashed, timestamped capture is what the new capture workflow (tools/capture_official.py) is built to keep, daily, once it runs on GitHub's runners.

item: Two hand-written depth figures disagreed with the tool that produces them, and one depth match is by name only
detail: The README and research/depth-and-deficiency.md published 57 of 76 Out or Doubtful players on a club chart and 40 at depth 1, and cited this flag as F-19. The depth tool's own output held 58 at the committed snapshot, so the prose did not match the tool it cited, and F-19 is the staking flag, not the depth one. Michael Burton (CLE) is matched by name only. The injury report lists him as FB, Calf, Out; the club's chart lists a Michael Burton at RB, depth 3, Out, Calf. The match counts him toward the 62 on-chart figure and he does not enter any starter count, because depth 3 is not a starter.
why: A figure in prose must come from the run that produced the data. The README and the depth note now quote the rebuilt values (62 of 81 on chart; 41 at depth 1, 23 offense and 18 defense; 20 clubs with a starter out or doubtful; 20 unmatched; two holes; zero cascades) and cite F-25. The Burton match is left in place and flagged: a reviewer should confirm from the club's own page whether the chart's RB row is the same man the report lists at FB before the join is treated as exact.

item: The NFL.com reserve-list reads disagree with each other, so 'not listed' cannot be read as 'available'
detail: Two official reads of the November 2026 reserve-list page disagree. The 2026-11-14 capture held 17 rows, dated 11/07 to 11/12, and included Michael Wilson (ARI, 11/10). The 2026-11-17 read holds 25 rows, dated 11/10 to 11/17, and does not include Wilson or any 11/07, 11/08 or 11/09 entry. Malik Willis (MIA, 11/10) is in both reads and is confirmed on NFL.com's own article (see F-44 and the register).
why: A reserve-list read that drops rows cannot prove a player is absent from the list, and a player missing from the list is not evidence he is healthy. The cause is not determined from this sandbox: the page may show a fixed number of rows per view, or the reader may not have followed a pagination control. Until the page's controls are checked and the list is captured in full, the reserve list is used only as evidence of a listing, never as proof of absence. Transcription: research/verification/official-reserve-list-2026-11-17.csv (25 rows).

item: Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley: NFL.com articles say both were placed on injured reserve, but neither is on the November reserve-list reads
detail: NFL.com reported on 1 Nov 2026 that Jesse Minter said Jackson 'will be placed on injured reserve' (at least four games). A later NFL.com article says 'With Jackson and Tyler Huntley placed on injured reserve, the Ravens were forced to start undrafted third-stringer Joe Fagnano'. Neither name appears on the NFL.com November reserve-list read of 2026-11-17 or on the 2026-11-14 capture.
why: Two official NFL.com records disagree on whether two players are on IR. The articles are reporting; the reserve list is the transaction record. Until the reserve list shows both names, or a transaction record says otherwise, the IR status is carried as reported and not as a confirmed transaction. F-43 (incomplete reads) is the likeliest explanation to test first, but no cause is established here.

item: Re-confirmed on 2026-11-17: the Texans depth chart is an image only, labelled 'Unofficial Depth Chart', so no structured source exists for the Texans row
detail: The Texans' depth-chart page, read 2026-11-17 (https://www.houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart), carries the chart as an image and labels it 'Unofficial Depth Chart'. item: No immutable multi-day availability capture history exists on this branch: data/captures/ is absent, and the capture workflow runs from the default branch
detail: data/captures/ does not exist in the repository, so the repository holds no raw, hashed, dated capture of the injury report or any club depth page. The capture workflow (.github/workflows/capture.yml) is scheduled on the default branch and has run four times there, and all four runs failed before any capture was stored (see F-48).
why: The brief requires a multi-day history so practice designations can be replayed as they were known. One reading cannot support that. Until the capture workflow completes on main and commits captures, the requirement is not met and must not be described as met. The first step is the failing line in the run log (F-48).

item: The official-capture workflow has failed on all four of its runs on main, so no capture has been stored
detail: The capture workflow (.github/workflows/capture.yml), which fetches the NFL.com injury report and the 32 club depth-chart pages every six hours, has four runs on main, and all four concluded failure: 2026-11-16 06:40 UTC (run 43818369872), 2026-11-16 22:13 UTC (run 43967865851), 2026-11-17 08:00 UTC (run 44043083196), and 2026-11-17 21:00 UTC (run 44175196682). In each run the step 'Fetch, schema-check and store the official pages' failed, and the verification, freshness and commit steps were skipped. The job log could not be downloaded from the sandbox (the archive download returned an end-of-file error), so the failing line is not read here.
why: Candidate causes, none confirmed: (a) an HTTP error or timeout on any of the 33 fetches (the injury page and 32 club pages), which the tool records as a failure; (b) the depth schema check, which requires a table tag in the raw HTML of every club page, while Houston publishes its chart as an image (F-24) and may carry no table; (c) the injury schema check, which requires the week heading and at least 28 'Practice Status' and 28 'Game Status' markers. The owner should open the failing run on GitHub, read the failing line, fix the check or the fetch, run the workflow manually, and confirm a stored capture and a passing freshness step. Until then there is no multi-day history, and the immutability requirement is not met.

item: Side bets were settled on the straight-up winner, not on the spread: one recorded result is wrong (Week 9, CLE +4.5)
detail: tools/origination.py (lines 575-578) settles a side bet by comparing the straight-up margin with the pick, not with the selected team's closing line. Week 9, Browns at Saints (ESPN event 401873039; official NFL.com final: CLE 22 - NO 23, overtime): the recorded Browns +4.5 side bet at -105 is graded lost. Against its own closing line it covers (margin -1, plus 4.5, equals +3.5) and is won. Across the 12 graded bets the recorded record is 8-4, +2.082 units, +17.351% ROI; re-settled it is 9-3, +4.035 units, +33.621% ROI. Only one of the 12 outcomes changes. The corrected figure is on luck.html. signal-vs-staking.html still shows the uncorrected 2.082 units and 17.351% ROI per bet, with no note that a settlement error changes it.
why: This is a settlement error, not a change of rule, so it is corrected rather than argued. The recorded graded file is not edited, so the original record stays auditable. n = 12 bets over four games: neither ROI is evidence of skill, and a cluster interval would span zero. Requested for the integration owner: label the uncorrected figure as superseded on signal-vs-staking.html, or re-grade and republish with a dated note. Not changed in this session, because the graded file and the page generator belong to the origination build. Reproducible: tools/settlement_recheck.py re-settles all 12 bets from the committed files, without reusing luck.py.

item: An earlier count of six graded mismatches was wrong: the independent re-check reproduces one

It is recorded here so the correction is visible. tools/settlement_recheck.py re-derives all 12 bets without tools/luck.py and reproduces luck.json exactly: 2.0821 units and 17.351% recorded; 4.0345 units and 33.621% re-settled.
